# Jubilees Chapter 24 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac, the Wells, and the Birthright

---

**24:1** After Abraham died, the LORD blessed his son Isaac. Isaac left Hebron and settled near the well of the vision, at the start of the forty-third jubilee.

**24:2** Soon after, a second famine struck the land — different from the one in Abraham's time. Isaac went to Gerar to see the king of the Philistines, Abimelech.

**24:3** The LORD appeared to Isaac and said: "Don't go down to Egypt. Stay in the land I'm pointing you to. Live there, and I'll be with you and bless you. I will give all these lands to you and your descendants, just as I swore to your father Abraham. I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore.

**24:4** Your descendants will inherit all this land, and every nation on earth will find blessing through them — because Abraham listened to me and kept everything I asked of him: my commands, my statutes, my laws."

**24:5** Isaac settled in Gerar for twenty-one years.

**24:6** Abimelech told his people that Isaac was his brother — he was afraid to touch him because of Isaac's wife Rebekah, who was beautiful.

**24:7** Isaac thrived in Philistine territory. He built up huge flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and donkeys. He farmed the land and got a hundredfold return. He kept growing richer and richer until the Philistines became deeply envious of him.

**24:8** Back when Abraham was alive, his servants had dug many wells. But after Abraham died, the Philistines had plugged them all up and filled them with dirt.

**24:9** So Abimelech told Isaac: "You need to leave. You've grown more powerful than us." Isaac moved away from Gerar and settled in the nearby valleys.

**24:10** There he uncovered the old wells his father's servants had dug — the ones the Philistines had blocked up — and restored them, giving them back the same names Abraham had given them.

**24:11** Then Isaac's servants dug a new well in the valley and hit spring water. But the herdsmen of Gerar showed up and fought over it: "That water is ours." Isaac named that well Esek — Quarrel — because they had quarreled with him there.

**24:12** His servants dug another well. The Philistines fought over that one too. Isaac called it Sitnah — Hostility.

**24:13** He moved again and dug a third well. This time no one came to fight over it. Isaac named it Rehoboth — Wide Open Space — and said, "Finally the LORD has given us room, and we can thrive in this land."

**24:14** From there Isaac traveled back up to Beersheba — the well of the oath.

**24:15** That night the LORD appeared to him: "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid. I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants — for Abraham my servant's sake."

**24:16** Isaac built an altar there and worshipped the LORD. He set up camp, and his servants dug a well.

**24:17** That same day, Abimelech's envoys came to Isaac and said: "Let's make a treaty — a formal oath between your people and ours. We never hurt you, we only did you good, and we let you leave in peace. God is clearly with you."

**24:18** Isaac said, "Why are you here? You despised me and drove me out." They answered: "We can see with our own eyes that the LORD is with you. That's why we're asking for this treaty — swear that you won't harm us, just as we never harmed you, only treated you well and let you leave peacefully. You are blessed by the LORD."

**24:19** Isaac threw a feast for them. They ate and drank together, and that same day they swore the oath. Then Isaac sent them off and they parted on good terms.

**24:20** That very same day, Esau came dragging himself in from the fields, completely famished. He said to his brother Jacob, "Give me some of that red stuff — that stew." Jacob said, "Sell me your birthright first."

**24:21** Esau said, "I'm dying here — what good is a birthright to a dead man?" Jacob said, "Then swear it to me right now." Esau swore, and he sold his birthright to Jacob.

**24:22** Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. Esau ate, drank, got up, and walked away. He didn't care at all about the birthright he'd just handed over.

**24:23** In the first year of the seventh week, Isaac again sowed in Philistine territory and harvested a hundredfold. He kept growing, becoming more and more prosperous.

**24:24** In the second year of the seventh week, famine spread across the whole land — everywhere except the Philistine territories.

**24:25** The Philistines' envy of Isaac's livestock and wealth continued to grow.

**24:26** Finally Abimelech said bluntly: "Everything you have really belongs to us anyway. Get out of our land."

**24:27** Isaac left and went into the valley, where he dug his wells once more.

**24:28** That is how things stood in those days.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Isaac is a transitional figure in Jubilees — echoing Abraham (famine, wife-sister deception, wells, Abimelech) while preparing for Jacob. The birthright scene (vv.20-22) is pointedly flat — Esau's despising of the birthright is matter-of-fact. "Three weeks of years" = 21 years rendered explicitly.*
